sentences.text: This animal featured a long, tubular snout that was wider than it was tall.
Its narrow shape suggests it ate fish, yet the skull measured exactly 38 cm long, which was too small for large pycnodonts like Phacodus.
Scientists propose the type specimen was a small adult or subadult that may have lived in freshwater to survive the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
A cladistic analysis by Jouve and colleagues classified Ocepesuchus as a gavialoid.
It lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
